activities.anchor: found the plate fogged where the salts had sat
activities.caption: bet before you read on — what crossed the drawer?
activities.name: repBecqPredict

config.q: Something crossed the drawer and altered chemistry through the wrapper. What kind of thing was it?
choices: A faint glow the eye had just missed
An invisible emission that ionises matter — undetectable by any sense
A chemical vapour rising from the jar
Warmth seeping from the drawer's wood
config.why: Nothing seeable, hearable, smellable or touchable — and exposure triggers no nerve impulses, so in this discipline the instrument is the only witness.

activities.anchor: past bismuth-209 no configuration is stable at all
activities.caption: the tug-of-war verdicts — file each nucleus
activities.name: repStableSort

config.prompt: The tug-of-war verdicts — file each nucleus:
buckets: wrong ratio or too much mass — must shed energy

items.label: helium-4 — two and two, a very tightly bound package
carbon-14 — a neutron excess waiting to convert
uranium-238 — far too much mass to hold
any nucleus too heavy for balance — every arrangement emits

config.why: Light elements favour equal numbers; heavy ones need extra neutrons as glue; past the last balanced nuclide, every configuration sheds its excess by emitting.

activities.caption: pair each decay mode with its repair job
activities.name: repDecayMatch

config.prompt: Four repair routes — pair each decay mode with what it does:

pairs.right: ejects a helium-4 nucleus — mass and proton count drop together
a neutron converts to a proton; an electron and an antineutrino fly out
a proton converts to a neutron — the fix for the opposite imbalance
no particle, no identity change — the excited daughter sheds pure energy

config.why: Each mode repairs a specific defect — and the daughter's excited state is why gamma usually follows the others.

activities.caption: true or false — activity is not a danger dial
activities.name: repActivityJudge

statements.s: Radioactivity is a substance property: the more radioactive, the more dangerous.
statements.why: It is an event rate — hazard depends on what is emitted, at what energy, and where the source sits.

statements.s: A weak beta emitter and a strong gamma emitter at the same event rate are equally hazardous.
statements.why: Identical counts, very different dangers — the number on the counter begins the safety analysis, it does not end it.

statements.s: Hazard analysis starts with three questions: how many events, over what time, measured with what.
statements.why: The discipline's own habit — activity, energy and location all modify the verdict.

statements.s: Radioactivity is an event rate, not a danger dial.
statements.why: The reason hazard needs the whole physics, never one number.

config.root: A proposal reaches the waste desk: dissolve spent fuel in acid and chemically bind the hazard away. Walk the analysis.

start.text: The proposal rests on one assumption. Which?

choices.label: Radioactivity is a chemical property, removable by chemistry
Given enough heat, the decay rate rises

chem.text: Chemistry rearranges electrons; decay happens in the nucleus, a hundred thousand times deeper. The proposal attacks the wrong storey of the building.

choices.label: So what can change the rate?

heat.text: λ is fixed by nuclear structure — independent of temperature, pressure and bonds. That is why decay heat cannot be switched off.

nothing.text: Storage, not treatment — the timetable is nuclear and unbudgeable.

config.why: The decay constant ignores temperature, pressure and chemistry alike — so the engineering answer is containment on the exponential's own schedule.

activities.anchor: the photon converts into an electron and a positron in the nuclear field
activities.caption: assemble the neutron shield, source outward
activities.name: repShieldOrder

config.prompt: Build the neutron shield, from the source outward:
items: A hydrogenous layer — water, plastic, concrete — slows the fast neutrons (best off nuclei of similar mass)
A boron layer captures the slowed neutrons — the legendary absorber (cadmium too)
Lead or concrete behind, to catch the capture gammas
config.why: Uncharged neutrons ignore electron clouds and interact only with nuclei — slow them, absorb them, then catch the secondary photons, in that order.

activities.anchor: the most locally damaging radiation there is
activities.caption: drag across one alpha source, two addresses
activities.name: repAlphaCompare

config.prompt: Drag across one alpha source — same isotope, two addresses:

before.label: outside the body
before.text: A sheet of paper — or the dead outer layer of skin — stops it. A few centimetres in air, nothing through the surface: at arm's length, the harmless one.

after.label: inside the body
after.text: Inhaled or ingested, it deposits all its energy within a few microns of living tissue, no dead layer in the way — the worst-case internal hazard.

config.why: Same physics, opposite verdicts — which is why protection rules care so much about preventing intake.

activities.anchor: the answer is usually not a broken instrument but an under-counted average
activities.caption: guess the magnitude — counts to ±1 per cent
activities.name: repCountEstimate

config.prompt: Your counter has recorded N events. How many counts does the statistical uncertainty need to reach ±1 per cent?
config.why: The uncertainty of a count N is about √N, so the fractional error is 1/√N: one per cent needs the square root to be a hundred.
config.context: 100 counts → ±10 per cent; 10,000 counts → ±1 per cent.
